provenance: Root-reviewed synthetic literals; inherited wire/transfer/write vectors remain unchanged from qualified .005. Header vectors independently checked against pinned source scalar fields. No asset bytes or provider implementation used.

wire_target.returns: slash followed by unchanged ASCII encoded path
wire_target.refusal: ValueError with generic message and no raw path echo
preserves: valid percent-escape spelling and hex case

transfer.late: final clock() >= deadline for every returned outcome
transfer.empty_framing: response.length == 0 is handled before the read-deadline gate
transfer.complete_hash: SHA256 of fully stored chunks on complete outcome; partial hash null
transfer.noncomplete_hash: complete hash null; partial hash SHA256 of fully stored chunks, including empty
transfer.storage_error: propagate OSError, no transfer result, caller retains and must close fd; do not retry after zero write

build_plan.refusal: exported Refusal with generic reason; no required diagnostic priority

fixture_adapter_rules.response_length: Nonnegative remaining framed byte count or null. read1(max_bytes) returns at most max_bytes, splitting a data step as needed; it decrements framed length by returned byte count. EOF leaves any positive framing remainder unchanged.
fixture_adapter_rules.response_steps: A data step advances only when fully served; clock_when_fully_served then updates the fake clock. eof returns empty bytes; raises throws the named authored exception. No real HTTP object is created.
fixture_adapter_rules.clock: Returns initial_value until a data-step update; no prescribed number of clock() calls. Equality at deadline counts late.
fixture_adapter_rules.storage: Runner supplies an initially empty caller-owned temporary fd and compares physical stored bytes before caller cleanup. write_plan short writes must actually store the reported bytes.
fixture_adapter_rules.write_fn: write_fn(fd, bytes-like-buffer) -> int excluding bool in 1..remaining; zero/invalid/overlarge counts raise OSError without retry.
fixture_adapter_rules.read_effects: No fixed read call count is imposed except an explicitly forbidden read/EOF lookahead. Assert no read request after the named exhausted cap and retain the scripted unread payload.
fixture_adapter_rules.wire_errors: ValueError class and generic-no-echo policy are fixed; exact message text is not prescribed.

additional_policy.wire: Only ASCII URI segment characters A-Z a-z 0-9 -._~ ! $ & apostrophe ( ) * + , ; = : @ and valid percent escapes, separated by single slash. Reject literal backslash, leading/trailing/repeated slash and literal dot/dotdot segments. Preserve valid escapes without decoding or re-encoding.
additional_policy.precedence: framed remaining length zero; declared length over body cap; deadline; aggregate exhausted; body cap exhausted; bounded read. Final late flag applies independently.
additional_policy.arguments: ValueError for invalid shape/types/negative limits or nonfinite deadline; header kind must be exact str bmp/tga/unknown and prefix exact bytes. Limits and response.length exclude bool.
additional_policy.write: Invalid progress raises OSError. EINTR may retry; no retry after zero. Returned transfer hashes cover fully stored chunks only. The caller records any uncertain partial chunk after a storage exception.

steps.message: read1 forbidden for known empty frame

write_controls.applicability: Inject a genuinely positive short write when the candidate requests more than one byte. A valid byte-at-a-time implementation may have no such callback opportunity; retain exact result/storage checks and report that short-write path as not exercised, not as observed fault evidence.

write_controls.note: If the first write request exceeds one byte this is a mid-chunk error; if not, it is a completed one-byte chunk followed by error. No result/hash/count is fabricated on either exception path.

Static unlinked global slots stay inventoried; zero-face linked slots are not filtered.
Animated true is a node-key fact; hook/placement/cache/GL predicates remain unobserved.
